evidence: Plan: 'FunctionModel, which accepts a tools-less request over a tool_use history; the provider protocol constraint is unrepresented offline.'
Plan: 'LIVE-proven end to end: a deliberately tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls...(experiments exp_g/exp_h, recorded on [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] 2026-08-05)'
All six ACs drive a FunctionModel run; none exercises the live provider boundary that produced the original 400.
findings.finding: The bug was LIVE-proven on Bedrock and the fix was LIVE-proven end-to-end (exp_g/exp_h), but every acceptance criterion is a FunctionModel/offline test — the exact substrate the plan itself blames for missing the original bug ('FunctionModel...accepts a tools-less request over a tool_use history; the provider protocol constraint is unrepresented offline'). No AC exercises the new steering path against the live Bedrock/Anthropic Converse boundary, so the AC set can go green while the provider still rejects the request shape. The live proof exists but is narrative in the Approach section, not encoded as a completion check.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria / Approach ('LIVE-proven end to end...exp_g/exp_h')
scenarios: A future regression to the tool surface passes all offline ACs but re-triggers the Bedrock ValidationException 400 in production, undetected by the AC set.
findings.suggested_fix: Promote the exp_g/exp_h live results into an [operator-attested] acceptance criterion referencing the recorded change id/timestamp, satisfying the E6(f) live-exercise requirement without a re-run.

findings.checklist_item: Add a live/end-to-end acceptance criterion (or a named/tracked LIVE regression check) that exercises the steering wrapper against a real Bedrock/Anthropic Converse request and asserts the request is protocol-valid (tools/toolConfig present) past the limit — the offline FunctionModel tests by the plan's own admission cannot represent the constraint that produced the 400.
evidence: Plan: 'the provider protocol constraint is unrepresented offline'

findings.finding: The bug is a real-provider protocol constraint (Bedrock/Anthropic reject tools-less requests over tool_use history) that the plan states is 'unrepresented offline' under FunctionModel — yet every acceptance criterion and test is satisfiable via FunctionModel, so the suite can go green without the real provider boundary ever exercising the fix. The end-to-end proof (exp_g/exp_h LIVE runs) is cited as prior evidence, not codified as a repeatable/acceptance gate.
findings.location: Testing / Acceptance Criteria; 'Why tests miss it' paragraph
scenarios: A future refactor re-empties the advertised tool surface only under a code path that FunctionModel accepts but Bedrock/Anthropic reject — the offline suite stays green and the regression ships
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC codifying the exp_g/exp_h LIVE result as a repeatable gate (e.g. a marked live test on [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]) asserting a post-limit request to the real provider succeeds and carries non-empty toolConfig, so the provider constraint is regression-protected rather than only historically observed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback when a steered model keeps calling tools instead of landing: name the existing backstop (e.g. eff_max_iter / UsageLimitExceeded) as the terminal bound and state the resulting outcome, or add an AC pinning terminal behavior for a model that ignores the steering notice.
evidence: Plan: 'Tool definitions stay advertised for the whole run ... the model lands naturally through the existing output path.'
Because tool defs remain advertised past the limit, the model is free to re-call tools; every re-call gets the same steering result rather than a real one, but nothing forces landing.

Landing is LIVE-proven only for cooperative models ('a deliberately tool-happy agent landed cleanly after 3 real + 7 steered calls'); the non-cooperative case (model keeps calling after N steered results) is unaddressed.

A step-budget backstop exists (structured_run.py:58 interpret_failure handles UsageLimitExceeded) but the plan never co-locates it as the fallback for steering-ignored runs, and the runaway detector is explicitly out of scope.
findings.finding: The steering notice is advisory-only and tool definitions stay advertised for the entire run by design, so a model that ignores the steering result can keep calling tools indefinitely; the plan does not specify the fallback that bounds a model which never lands after being steered.
findings.location: Approach paragraph ('the model lands naturally through the existing output path'); AC line 3 (a run that exceeds the limit still lands a final output)
scenarios: A model that treats the steering tool result as a transient error and re-issues the same/other tool calls, spinning through steered results until some other limit trips.
